records.label: managerial or organizational leader of
records.definition: Person X holds a managerial or organizational leadership office in organization or political body Y.
records.scope_notes: President, leader, head, manager and executive paths dominate. This preserves the prior broad leadership scope, including historical office. Truncated political labels remain identity ambiguities; mere membership and event attendance do not suffice.

records.label: directed communication to
records.definition: X directs an utterance, request, warning or explicit message to Y.
records.scope_notes: Tell, urge, ask, notify and speak-to give the directed-communication component, preserving prior scope. Accusing or speaking about someone is insufficient without evidence of address. Sending an unspecified object alone is ambiguous; institutional speech through representatives is allowed.

records.label: analyst at
records.definition: Person X works as an analyst for or follows an industry or companies for organization Y.
records.scope_notes: Analyst-at/with/for dominates, preserving the prior analyst scope. Professorship, directorship or expertise alone does not establish an analyst role; these form competing components.

records.label: coach of
records.definition: Person X coaches sports team or collegiate athletic program Y.
records.scope_notes: Coach descriptions dominate, retaining the prior coach scope and direction. Historical coaching qualifies; a managerial title alone would not establish coaching, and player or institutional-membership roles remain separate.

records.label: has organizational or political leader
records.definition: Organization or political body X has person Y as a leader or holder of a leadership office.
records.scope_notes: Possessive leader/president and inverse leader appositions dominate. This is the inverse direction of the prior leadership predicate, explicitly X body to Y person. Ordinary membership, geographic co-occurrence and interaction alone do not qualify.

records.label: managerial or organizational leader of
records.definition: Person X holds a managerial or organizational leadership office in organization Y.
records.scope_notes: Director and head paths dominate, preserving the prior broad managerial scope for director clusters. Departmental or research directorship qualifies; economist, lobbyist and academic roles alone do not. Inverse organization-to-president paths are separate.

records.label: subsidiary or organizational unit of
records.definition: Organization X is owned by, a subsidiary of, or an organizational unit of parent Y.
records.scope_notes: Unit, part, subsidiary and owned-by define the child-to-parent containment predicate, retaining prior scope. This cluster includes many office-location attachments: a city label may be shorthand for an omitted local office, but the literal city is not the organizational unit, so those cases require identity clarification.

records.label: member of
records.definition: Person, country or organization X is or becomes a member of organization or political group Y.
records.scope_notes: Member-of, membership, entry/accession and join provide the membership component. Joining someone in an action or alliance is distinct from becoming a constituent member; bare join without its completion can be ambiguous. Diplomatic relations, borders and television-title fragments do not establish membership.

records.label: spokesperson for
records.definition: Person X serves as a spokesperson or expressly speaks for person or organization Y.
records.scope_notes: Spokesman/spokeswoman is the strongest recurring specific role and preserves the prior spokesperson predicate. This cluster also contains a substantial broader managerial/director component; those offices alone do not imply a spokesperson role, and this scope does not union them. Predicate choice is material in this mixed cluster.

records.label: winner or champion of
records.definition: Person, team or organization X wins award or competitive title/event Y.
records.scope_notes: Win, champion, winner and title paths define the coherent award/championship component, preserving the prior scope. Political office, organizational membership and travel are separate predicates; participation alone does not qualify. A clear win path is assessed as textual support without importing external outcome history.

records.label: politically controls
records.definition: Political group X controls or gains control of political body Y.
records.scope_notes: Control, take-control, retain-control, win-control and regain-control collectively define the coherent political-control component. Generic win/be-in and sporting tournament paths form competing components; they are not combined into a generic success relation. Winning control or historical control qualifies, mere presence or membership does not.

records.label: directed communication to
records.definition: X directs an utterance, request, advice or explicit message to Y.
records.scope_notes: Ask, tell, urge, persuade and address-to form the dominant communication component, preserving prior scope. Unspecified send, submit or give objects are ambiguous alone because they can be noncommunicative. Sporting player roles do not independently establish communication.

records.label: owns
records.definition: Person or organization X owns organization or asset Y.
records.scope_notes: Own, owner, parent, company-of and acquisition paths collectively form the largest coherent ownership component, preserving the prior ownership direction. Birthplace is a prominent competing component with the two highest individual path counts; it is not unioned with ownership. Location of premises alone is insufficient and proposed/rejected acquisitions alone would be ambiguous.

records.label: lives in
records.definition: Person or population X resides in geographic place Y.
records.scope_notes: Live-in dominates the coherent residence component, preserving prior scope. An explicit home or immigration/resettlement can establish residence; death or other events in a place alone cannot. Bare adjectives or malformed names do not identify a stable person automatically.

records.label: economist at
records.definition: Person X is an economist affiliated with organization Y.
records.scope_notes: Economist-at/for/with/of dominates the occupational component. Generic official, diplomat, analyst, executive or specialist roles alone do not establish economist status. Departmental affiliation and historical service qualify.

records.label: defeated opponent
records.definition: X defeated opponent Y in a competitive contest.
records.scope_notes: Beat, defeat, victory-over, sweep and outlast collectively define the dominant victory component, retaining the prior directional defeat scope. Lose-to and play paths are competing or weaker relations; a win remains supported despite losses on other occasions.

records.label: organization based or located in
records.definition: Organization X is based, headquartered or physically located in geographic place Y.
records.scope_notes: Based-in, headquarters-in and geographic company/firm descriptions dominate, preserving the prior organizational-location scope. Geographic noun modifiers qualify for firms; subject-matter or industry modifiers and personal/event locations alone do not.

records.label: departed from
records.definition: Person or organization X leaves or withdraws physically from geographic place Y.
records.scope_notes: This diffuse cluster mixes departure, arrival, legal occupation, publication and residence paths. Leave, withdraw-from, withdrawal and pull-out collectively define the selected coherent departure component. Arrival is a competing direction and residence is a different predicate; neither is unioned into it. No uniquely dominant interpretation is guaranteed, so relation-level predicate choice is a material caveat.

records.label: subsidiary or organizational unit of
records.definition: Organization X is owned by, a subsidiary of, or an organizational unit of parent Y.
records.scope_notes: Unit-of, part-of, owned-by and subsidiary-of dominate, preserving the prior child-to-parent organizational containment predicate. Historical ownership qualifies; competition and geographical containment do not.

records.label: managerial or organizational leader of
records.definition: Person X holds a managerial or organizational leadership office in organization or political body Y.
records.scope_notes: Chairman, head, executive and leader paths dominate, preserving the prior broad leadership scope. Founder, ownership and ordinary membership alone are separate relations. Party adjectives and party-labelled unnamed persons remain identity ambiguities.

records.label: criticized or accused
records.definition: Argument 1 publicly criticized, blamed or accused argument 2.
records.scope_notes: This is a highly mixed dictionary: accuse/criticize/blame is the selected coherent family; joining/voting together, numerical comparisons, legal representation and ownership compete. A warning without criticism, general communication or simple rivalry alone does not establish this predicate. Label selection is materially uncertain.

records.label: resided in
records.definition: Person or population 1 resides or formerly resided in geographic place 2.
records.scope_notes: Live/resident/residence and explicit resettlement qualify. Visiting, travel, work, officeholding and citizenship alone do not establish residence.

records.label: coach of
records.definition: Person 1 is or was a coach of sports team/program 2.
records.scope_notes: Explicit coach title or coaching verb qualifies, including historical/dismissed roles. Manager/president alone, authorship and geographic movement are distinct predicates.

records.label: managerial or political leadership in
records.definition: Person 1 holds or formerly held a managerial or political leadership office in organization/body 2.
records.scope_notes: Head, chair, president, director, chief and leader qualify, including a leadership office within a subunit. Mere committee membership, founder/owner status or analyst role does not.

records.label: defeated
records.definition: Argument 1 defeated argument 2 in an explicit sporting, electoral or other contest.
records.scope_notes: Choose beat/victory-over/sweep/outlast from this mixed dictionary. Playing, losing, transfers, speaking and residence are distinct predicates. Generic historical victories count without requiring every row to express the win.

records.label: has spokesperson
records.definition: Organization or political body 1 has person 2 as its spokesperson.
records.scope_notes: Inverse spokesperson-to-principal direction, selected from the repeated spokesman appositions and spokesman-at-briefing paths. President, leader, secretary or lawyer alone does not prove a spokesperson role. Political government/leader paths are a substantial competing theme.

records.label: organization located or based in
records.definition: Organization 1 is based in or has headquarters, offices or a campus in geographic place 2.
records.scope_notes: Explicit organizational site/base paths qualify; personal employment, coaching, award events and ownership are separate relations.

records.label: managerial leadership in
records.definition: Person 1 holds or formerly held a managerial leadership office in organization 2.
records.scope_notes: Director/head family dominates, with chair, president and manager paraphrases. Spokesperson, lawyer or aide alone does not establish leadership; names known-as and geographic relations are competing themes.

records.label: organization located or based in
records.definition: Organization 1 is based in or has offices/sites in geographic place 2.
records.scope_notes: Company/firm-in, based-in and geographic noun compounds qualify. Personal residence/death, organizational employers and industry/Internet compounds are other relations. Nationality alone is ambiguous.

records.label: managerial or political leadership in
records.definition: Person 1 holds or formerly held a managerial or political leadership office in organization/body 2.
records.scope_notes: Head, president, leader, chair, executive, manager, director and chief qualify. Founder, generic employee, coach or organizational subsidiary alone does not. Historical offices qualify.

records.label: lawyer or attorney for
records.definition: Person 1 is or was a lawyer or attorney serving principal, organization or jurisdiction 2.
records.scope_notes: Includes legal employment at a firm and government attorney offices for a jurisdiction. Merely working as a lawyer in a city may establish place of practice but not representation of that city; review jurisdiction ambiguity. Travel, sports and corporate nationality are competing predicates.

records.label: organizational subsidiary or unit of
records.definition: Organization 1 is or was a subsidiary, division, owned organization or unit of parent 2.
records.scope_notes: Child-to-parent direction. Explicit unit/parent/owned-by evidence qualifies, including partial and historical ownership. Personal roles, location, disease and family relations do not.

records.label: analyst for
records.definition: Person 1 is or was an analyst for organization 2.
records.scope_notes: Explicit analyst and following/tracking an industry for an employer qualify. Economist/strategist alone is a role-scope ambiguity; managerial, professorial or other roles alone are not analyst roles.

records.label: organizational subsidiary or unit of
records.definition: Organization 1 is or was a subsidiary, division, owned organization or unit of parent 2.
records.scope_notes: Child-to-parent direction; partial or historical ownership and institutional units qualify. Geographic sites, employment and reverse parent-to-child relations do not automatically qualify.

records.label: owns
records.definition: Argument 1 owns or previously owned company, organization or asset 2.
records.scope_notes: Owner/parent, completed acquisitions and explicit partial ownership qualify in owner-to-asset direction. Managing, publishing, proposing/rejecting a merger and political office alone do not.

records.label: winner or champion of
records.definition: Argument 1 won competition/award 2 or holds its championship.
records.scope_notes: The win/champion family dominates identifiable semantics; movement and presence are substantial competing themes. Mere participation, reaching an event or winning one stage does not imply winning the whole event. Political office is outside this preserved award/competition scope.

records.label: managerial or political leadership in
records.definition: Person 1 holds or formerly held a managerial or political leadership office in organization/body 2.
records.scope_notes: Chair, president, executive, head, director, chief and political leader qualify. Founder/owner alone does not. Historical offices qualify. Direction person to organization.

records.label: communicated to
records.definition: Argument 1 addressed, contacted or sent a message to argument 2.
records.scope_notes: Tell, urge, ask, notify, speak-to and message/report recipient paths establish direction. Accusing or describing a person without addressing them is not enough. Sending something unspecified may require object/attachment review.

records.label: president or manager of
records.definition: Person 1 holds or formerly held president or manager office in organization 2.
records.scope_notes: Manager and president are the largest combined office families; professor/academic roles form a substantial competing theme. Preserve the prior president-or-manager scope: generic head, executive, director, coach, professor or expert alone does not establish these titles.

records.label: defeated
records.definition: Argument 1 defeated argument 2 in an explicit sporting, electoral or other contest.
records.scope_notes: Winner-to-loser direction. Historical wins qualify; merely playing, facing, trailing, leading standings or transferring players does not.

records.label: contributed writing to publication
records.definition: Argument 1 wrote, reviewed or worked as a critic for publication 2.
records.scope_notes: This highly mixed dictionary has several competing themes and no clean dominant predicate. After reading all 38 complete fact groups, choose the coherent write-in/critic-for/review-for family, also resolving say-in ambiguity toward publications where local evidence permits. Geographic residence/travel and lawyer-in-city are competing predicates. This labeling choice is a material uncertainty in the precision estimate. Mere being quoted in a publication does not establish authorship.

records.label: traveled or moved to
records.definition: Argument 1 traveled, relocated, returned or was transported to destination 2.
records.scope_notes: Direction toward the destination. Visits and historical movements qualify. Mere presence, residence, officeholding, or leaving/moving from the second argument alone does not. Unobserved modality is a corpus limitation.

records.label: athlete played for team
records.definition: Person 1 played as an athlete for sports team 2.
records.scope_notes: Team player/center/wing/guard/scorer membership and scoring for the team qualify. Coaching alone, merely leading an opponent, communication and corporate interactions do not.

records.label: managerial leadership in
records.definition: Argument 1 holds or formerly held a leadership office in organization 2.
records.scope_notes: Chairman and head dominate, with director, executive and president paraphrases. Founder/owner alone is insufficient. Explicit former office qualifies; nomination alone does not show office held.

records.label: defeated
records.definition: Argument 1 defeated argument 2 in a sporting, electoral or other explicit contest.
records.scope_notes: Historical wins qualify. Playing, facing, a period score or standings lead alone does not show a win. Preserve direction winner to loser.

records.label: analyst for
records.definition: Person 1 is or was an analyst for organization 2.
records.scope_notes: Explicit analyst titles and following/tracking an industry for the employer qualify. Economist, strategist or specialist without analyst evidence may require role-scope review; president/director/professor/lawyer alone do not establish this role.

records.label: political or organizational leader of
records.definition: Argument 1 is or was a political/organizational leader of group, legislature or political body 2.
records.scope_notes: Leader, head, chair and legislative leadership posts qualify. Mere candidacy, party membership or communicating to a body does not. Leadership in a legislature includes majority/minority leadership, not only heading the entire chamber.

records.label: organizational subsidiary or unit of
records.definition: Argument 1 is or was an organizational subsidiary, division, unit or owned organization of parent 2.
records.scope_notes: Direction subsidiary to parent. Explicit ownership qualifies, including partial ownership. Mere employment, a geographic base or business interaction does not.

records.label: president or manager of
records.definition: Argument 1 holds or formerly held the office of president or manager of organization 2.
records.scope_notes: The two dominant title families are president and manager, as in the prior evaluation. Generic executive, director, owner, coach or political leader alone does not establish either title.

records.label: has political leader or minister
records.definition: Political body, party, country or legislature 1 has or had person 2 as a leader, minister or senior political officeholder.
records.scope_notes: Direction body to leader, inverse of the dominant leader-of family. Legislature majority/minority leaders and whips qualify. Spokespeople, aides, visitors, merely cited officials elsewhere and the reverse direction do not.

records.label: communicated to
records.definition: Argument 1 addressed, contacted or sent a message to argument 2.
records.scope_notes: Tell, ask, urge, warn, write, talk and message recipient paths establish directed communication. Accusing or describing another person without addressing them is not enough. Sending a person somewhere is not sending them a message.

records.label: organization located or based in
records.definition: Organization 1 is based in or has headquarters, offices or a campus in geographic place 2.
records.scope_notes: Historical bases and explicit organizational sites qualify. People, award recipients, leadership offices and merely named-as paths are other predicates.

records.label: owns
records.definition: Argument 1 owns or previously owned company, organization or asset 2.
records.scope_notes: Parent, owner, acquisition and explicit partial ownership qualify in parent-to-child direction. Being born in a place, employment, management alone, or a proposed/rejected acquisition does not.

records.label: organization located or based in
records.definition: Organization 1 is based in or has a geographic office/site in place 2.
records.scope_notes: Firm/company-in and based-in paths qualify. Nationality adjectives alone remain ambiguous between geographic base and ownership/origin. Individual professionals, agencies as employers and sectors are other predicates.

records.label: lawyer or attorney for
records.definition: Argument 1 serves as a lawyer, attorney or legal counsel for organization or person 2, including employment at a law firm.
records.scope_notes: The aggregate lawyer/attorney/counsel family is chosen from a mixed professional-role dictionary. A professor, analyst, economist or director without legal representation evidence does not qualify. A firm partner without a legal-role attachment is ambiguous.

records.label: organization located or based in
records.definition: Organization 1 is based in or has an office/site in geographic place 2.
records.scope_notes: Firm/company-in, based-in, headquarters-in and geographic noun compounds qualify. Nationality adjective alone is ambiguous between ownership/origin and actual base. A sector, parent company or person is not a geographic place.

records.label: managerial leadership in
records.definition: Argument 1 is or was a person holding a managerial or leadership office in organization 2.
records.scope_notes: Choose the aggregate director/manager/president/chief family from the full dictionary. Spokesperson and economist are substantial competing roles, but employment alone does not establish leadership; a director role qualifies without requiring the chief executive.

records.label: coach of
records.definition: Person 1 is or was a coach of sports team or program 2.
records.scope_notes: Explicit coach titles and coaching verbs qualify, including historical or dismissed coaches. Playing, owning, managing without coaching evidence, and political leadership do not.

records.label: managerial leadership in
records.definition: Argument 1 holds or formerly held a managerial or leadership office in organization 2.
records.scope_notes: Head, president, chair, chief, executive, director and manager qualify. Founder, owner, generic employee or spokesperson alone do not. Historical offices qualify.

records.label: winner or champion of
records.definition: Argument 1 won competition or award 2 or holds its championship.
records.scope_notes: Historical wins and explicit award recipients qualify. Merely playing, reaching an event, winning an individual stage, or holding political office does not. Boxing title-body champion paths qualify under the same broad championship scope as earlier audits.

records.label: defeated opponent
records.definition: X defeated opposing competitor Y in at least one competitive contest; direction is winner to defeated opponent.
records.scope_notes: Preserves the previous defeated-opponent predicate. Explicit beat, defeat, victory over or completed sweep qualify. Losing, playing, facing, trading or standings alone do not. Different historical games can supply both wins and losses; a clear win supports the fact but other assignments remain mixed evidence.

records.label: president or manager of
records.definition: Person X holds or held an explicitly identified president or manager office in organization, team or institution Y.
records.scope_notes: Preserves the earlier combined president/manager scope. Explicit historical office qualifies. Generic leader, running/control, director, chairman, founder, owner, coach or athlete leadership alone does not establish either specified office. Manager cases are marked as the deliberately broader role family.

records.label: organizational leadership office in
records.definition: X holds or held an explicit managerial or leadership office in organization or institution Y, such as chairperson, head, chief, director, president or executive.
records.scope_notes: Preserves the prior managerial/leadership office predicate. Explicit named office qualifies. Founding, ownership, ordinary employment or attendance alone do not; generic athletic lead is not an organizational office. Membership, serving or sitting on a committee alone does not imply its leadership. A generic Democrat/Republican argument omits the individual officeholder and remains ambiguous under the same earlier rubric.

records.label: has spokesperson
records.definition: Organization or principal X has person Y serving as its spokesperson.
records.scope_notes: Reverse direction of spokesperson-for. Direct organization-modifying-spokesman plus appositive person evidence qualifies. Merely speaking at a building, secretary without press/spokesperson context, or kinship alone does not.

records.label: directed communication to
records.definition: X directs a communication, request, instruction, urging or submitted material to recipient Y.
records.scope_notes: Preserves the prior directed-communication scope. Tell, urge and submit-to qualify; a source speaking through its spokesperson has the spokesperson as intermediary, not automatically recipient. Meeting, visits and support alone are insufficient.

records.label: managerial or leadership office in
records.definition: X holds or held an explicit managerial or leadership office in organization or institution Y, such as chairperson, head, chief, director, president or executive.
records.scope_notes: Preserves the prior managerial/leadership office predicate. Explicit named office qualifies. Founding, ownership, ordinary employment or attendance alone do not; generic athletic lead is not an organizational office.

records.label: subsidiary or organizational unit of
records.definition: Organization or business unit X is a subsidiary, division, organizational part of, or owned business of parent organization Y.
records.scope_notes: Preserves the earlier subsidiary/unit/organizational-containment predicate. Explicit unit, subsidiary, division, part or owned-by evidence qualifies. Mere geography, employee affiliation or partial investment alone does not. A location name standing for an unnamed office is ambiguous rather than silently converted into an organization.

records.label: winner or champion of
records.definition: X won competition, race, championship, prize or award Y.
records.scope_notes: Preserves the earlier winner/champion scope, with Y the event or award, not the defeated opponent. Teams, people and racehorses can win. Participation or finishing alone is not sufficient; a historical win qualifies.

records.label: managerial or leadership office in
records.definition: X holds or held an explicit managerial or leadership office in organization or institution Y, such as chairperson, head, chief, director, president or executive.
records.scope_notes: Preserves the prior managerial/leadership office predicate. Explicit named office qualifies. Founding, ownership, ordinary employment or attendance alone do not; generic athletic lead is not an organizational office.

records.label: spokesperson for
records.definition: Person X serves or served as spokesperson for organization or principal Y.

records.label: managerial or leadership office in
records.definition: X holds or held an explicit managerial or leadership office in organization or institution Y, such as chairperson, head, chief, director, president or executive.
records.scope_notes: Preserves the prior managerial/leadership office predicate. Explicit named office qualifies. Founding, ownership, ordinary employment or attendance alone do not; generic athletic lead is not an organizational office.

records.label: defeated opponent

records.label: business or organization based or located in
records.definition: Business or organization X is based or physically located in geographic place Y.

Geographic noun modification can indicate a place, but nationality adjectives without a recoverable place and Wall Street used only as an industry label remain ambiguous; ordinary business association alone does not suffice.

records.label: coach of
records.definition: X is or was a coach of team, school or sporting program Y.
records.scope_notes: Preserves the previous coach predicate. Explicit coach role or coaching action qualifies, including a university/team named by its place. Mere athletic participation, ownership or general management does not.

records.label: leader or organizational head of
records.definition: X holds or held a leadership/head role in political body or organization Y.
records.scope_notes: Preserves the previous leader/head scope and includes recognized legislative leadership within a chamber, without requiring sole leadership of the whole body. Head/leader office qualifies; simple membership or founding alone does not.

records.label: owns or is parent of
records.definition: Person or organization X owns business, asset or organization Y, or is Y’s organizational parent.
records.scope_notes: This is the direction-reversed ownership family, distinct from subsidiary-of. Direct owns, owner or parent evidence qualifies. A mere partial stake or proposed acquisition is not silently treated as full ownership; direct ownership elsewhere can support the fact. Historical ownership qualifies.

records.label: subsidiary or organizational unit of
records.definition: Organization or business unit X is a subsidiary, division, organizational part of, or owned business of parent organization Y.
records.scope_notes: Preserves the earlier subsidiary/unit/organizational-containment predicate. Explicit unit, subsidiary, division, part or owned-by evidence qualifies. records.label: analyst at organization
records.definition: X is an analyst working at, with or for organization Y.
records.scope_notes: Preserves the prior analyst role rather than general employment. Explicit analyst affiliation qualifies; financial tracking can corroborate it. Economist-only or unclear attachment would be ambiguous, and another office alone would not suffice.

records.label: professor or university teacher at
records.definition: X is a professor or teaches at academic institution Y.

Explicit professor/teaches evidence supports a mixed case; a location or attendance alone does not.

records.label: leader or organizational head of
records.definition: X holds or held a leadership/head role in political body, party or organization Y.
records.scope_notes: Preserves prior leader/head scope, including legislative leadership within a chamber. Republican may name a party group when the named person is explicitly its leader; a singular nationality or truncated political label such as Soviet/Bosnian Serb does not automatically identify the organization. Membership alone does not establish leadership.

records.definition: X is an analyst working at, with or for organization Y.

records.label: chairperson of

records.label: coach of

records.label: defeated opponent

records.label: unit or subsidiary of

records.label: director of
records.definition: The first person is or was a director of the second organization.

records.label: economist affiliation
records.definition: The first person works or worked as an economist for the second organization.

records.label: political or organizational leader of

A generic political label is not a uniquely named person; incompatible personal names remain identity ambiguities. records.label: owner of
records.definition: The first person or organization owns or owned the second property, company, network or team.

records.label: director affiliation
records.definition: The first person holds or held a director role of, for, or at the second organization.
records.scope_notes: The director family overwhelmingly dominates, consistent with the specific-director scope of rel_263 and earlier reviews. Functional directors employed by an organization are included; this need not mean its sole overall leader. Professor, publisher, speaker, compiler or member alone is excluded. A truncated abstract topic requires identifying the intended institution.

records.label: directed communication
records.definition: The first person or institution communicates with, requests or urges action from, or advises the second.
records.scope_notes: Ask/urge/persuade/tell/notify form the coherent dominant communication family used previously. Bare cooperation or replacement is excluded. Send-to without a recoverable communicative object can be ambiguous. Institutional recipients are permitted.

records.label: managerial or leadership office in
records.definition: The first person holds or held an explicit managerial or leadership office in the second organization or governing body.

records.label: winner or champion of
records.definition: The first entity won the competition or award designated by the second, or held its championship title.
records.scope_notes: Win and winner dominate, using the same scope as rel_112 and the earlier reviews. A malformed appended path is not needed when clean direct evidence exists.

records.label: analyst at organization
records.definition: Person X is an analyst at, with or for organization Y.
records.scope_notes: Preserves specific analyst affiliation. Director, economist, strategist, partner or broad employment alone does not establish analyst; role/attachment ambiguity is kept explicit.

records.label: economist at organization
records.definition: Person X is an economist at, with, for or of organization Y.
records.scope_notes: Preserves economist-specific affiliation. Professor, president, analyst or strategist alone is insufficient; do not use external biography to fill an absent role.

records.label: organization based or located in
records.definition: Organization X is based, headquartered or physically located in geographical place Y.
records.scope_notes: Preserves organization-location scope. Explicit firm/company-in, based-in or headquarters evidence qualifies. Industry, personal residence/birth, nationality alone or non-place corporate affiliation does not.

records.label: managerial or leadership office in
records.definition: Person X holds or held an explicit managerial or leadership office in organization or institution Y, such as chairperson, head, director, president, manager, chief or executive.
records.scope_notes: Preserves prior organizational office family. The dictionary combines qualifying offices; founder, owner, analyst, ordinary employment or sporting lead alone is insufficient. Historical offices qualify.

records.label: subsidiary or organizational unit of
records.definition: Organization or business unit X is a subsidiary, division, owned business or organizational part of parent organization Y.
records.scope_notes: Preserves prior child-to-parent subsidiary/unit scope. Explicit part, unit, subsidiary or owned-by qualifies. Ordinary employment, a geographic site standing for an unnamed unit, and partial investment alone do not establish the same fact.

records.label: director of organization
records.definition: Person X holds or held an explicit director office in organization or institution Y.
records.scope_notes: Director-for/of/possessive/noun constructions are the leading family. Preserve the earlier director-specific scope. Spokesperson, adviser, confidante, lobbyist or chairwoman alone is a competing role; do not broaden to general affiliation.

records.label: managerial or leadership office in
records.definition: Person X holds or held an explicit managerial or leadership office in organization or institution Y, such as chairperson, head, director, president, manager, chief or executive.
records.scope_notes: Preserves prior organizational office family. The dictionary combines qualifying offices; founder, owner, analyst, ordinary employment or sporting lead alone is insufficient. Historical offices qualify.

records.label: leader or organizational head of
records.definition: Person X holds or held a leadership or head office in political body or organization Y.
records.scope_notes: Preserves prior leader/head scope, including legislative leadership and explicit president/chair office. Simple membership, founding, affiliation, legal representation or an athletic lead does not qualify.

records.label: defeated opponent
records.definition: X defeated opposing competitor Y in at least one competitive contest.
records.scope_notes: Preserves prior winner-to-opponent scope. Beat, defeat, completed sweep, outscore or victory over qualifies. Playing, facing, standings, losing, trades or transfers alone do not. A historical win remains supported when other rows describe losses; flag the mixed evidence.

records.scope_notes: Declare the coherent birthplace meaning from dominant born-in/born-into-family-in paths. Growing up, schooling, residence, nationality, work or later travel alone does not establish birthplace. This is a new explicit meaning where the prior common catalogue has no matching sampled relation.
